airport.name: Rio Grande do Norte/São Gonçalo do Amarante–Governador Aluízio Alves International Airport

summary: Natal’s Governador Aluízio Alves International Airport (IATA: NAT) opened in 2014 in São Gonçalo do Amarante, about 20 km northwest of downtown Natal. It replaced the older Augusto Severo airport and serves as the main gateway to Rio Grande do Norte’s beaches and dunes. The modern terminal is known for its compact, easy-to-navigate layout and regional artwork.
faqs:
Q: What is the airport code for Natal?
A: NAT is the IATA code; the airport is also known as Governador Aluízio Alves International Airport.

Q: How far is NAT from Natal city center?
A: It is roughly 20–25 km (12–15 miles) from central Natal, depending on traffic, with journeys typically taking 30–45 minutes.

Q: Is there public transportation to the airport?
A: Yes, local bus lines and executive/airport shuttle services connect the terminal to Natal and nearby areas; taxis and ride-hailing are also available.

Q: What facilities are available at NAT?
A: The terminal has shops, cafés, restaurants, car rental desks, ATMs, free Wi-Fi, and accessibility services.
transport_tips: Prepaid taxis and ride-hailing apps are the most straightforward options; confirm the pickup point outside arrivals. If using public buses, allow extra time because routes may require a transfer or have limited luggage space. Car rental agencies are located at the airport, and the drive to Ponta Negra or the city center takes about 30–45 minutes.
local_tip: Some navigation apps still point to the old Augusto Severo airport in Parnamirim, so double-check that your destination is São Gonçalo do Amarante before you leave.
